newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares end up, await tax reliefs.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end up, await tax reliefs.

text.p: Shares across India closed higher on Friday in anticipation of changes to a controversial tax proposal but volume was thin with investors reluctant to take large positions ahead of the weekend, brokers said.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram will address parliament on Monday about the proposed 1996/97 (April-March) budget, but any amendments to tax proposals may have to wait until September 9 or 10, a ministry official said in Delhi.
"The market will run out of steam if expectations do not materialise," said broker Sunil Kothari.
He said the expectations include exemption of company dividends from double taxation to lure retail investors to the stock markets.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index closed 21.00 points up at 3,514.61 after falling to 3,489.75 in early trade.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index gained 3.0 points to 1,029. Trading on the National bourse was lacklustre.
"We hardly got any business today," said Cyrus Rastomjee, dealer at brokerage El Dorado Guarantee. "Very dull."
Foreign and local fund buying in steel, cement and banking stocks helped the Delhi index add 3.21 points at 802.93.
The 100-share BSE National index advanced 1.10 points to 1,587.55. The Calcutta share index firmed 1.08 points to 450.58 and the Madras index rose 5.47 to 3,593.79.
On the BSE, TELCO was up 11.50 rupees at 509.75 and Bajaj Auto 6.50 at 1,058.50, but East India Hotels dropped 13 rupees to 647 and Indian Hotels 15.25 to 770.
Hindalco rose 9.0 rupees to 1,015.25, SBI 2.50 to 271.75, BSES 2.25 to 196.75, MTNL 3.75 to 207.75, Gujarat Ambuja Cement 2.50 to 324.50 and TISCO 0.50 to 195.50.
Hind Lever shed 8.25 rupees to 841.75, Grasim 5.25 to 442.25, ACC 2.75 to 2,157 and Colgate 3.25 to 259.50.
